unmapped_findings: For 12Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C the Vickers hardness is essentially unchanged relative to the hot-rolled state (401 HV -> 399 HV), despite full cellular transformation into α + κ-carbide coarse lamellae; Table 9 links this to the 'Wide' inter-lamellar spacing, whereas the 9Al-10Mn-1C 600 °C state with 'Narrow' spacing reaches 439 HV (b0051, b0096, b0107).

There is internal inconsistency in the paper's attribution of some 600 °C data: the Fig. 4 caption names 12Al-10Mn-1C while the accompanying Table 3 title names 9Al-10Mn-1C, and Table 4/Fig. 4 concern the 600 °C (not 800 °C) tempering of 12Al-10Mn-1C; these 600 °C data do not pertain to the 800 °C tempered sample (b0030, b0037, b0041, b0093).

The description of the 12Al-10Mn-1C 800 °C microstructure is partly conflicting in the text: b0107 states 'full cellular transformation into α + κ-carbide coarse lamellae, featuring high inter-lamellar spacing', whereas b0048 states γ grains present 'only early cellular transformed α + κ-carbide lamellae at their boundaries' (Fig. 5(b)); the Fig. 5(b) SEM image is separately described as a 'dense fine lamellar structure' (b0048, b0107, figure_005).

The paper hypothesises that 800 °C tempering triggered 'cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition', and describes metallic δ-ferrite branches linked to δ + κ-carbide lamellar grains extending inside spinodal decomposed γ grains, but this mixed-grain feature is reported specifically for 12Al-20Mn-1C (Fig. 14), not confirmed for 12Al-10Mn-1C (b0113, b0117, figure_014).

No CALPHAD phase-fraction diagram (Fig. 9, Fig. 12) was computed for the 12Al-10Mn-1C composition; the available diagrams cover 9Al-10Mn-0.4, 9Al-10Mn-1C, 9Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-30Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn-1C, so no computational/thermodynamic data could be attributed to this sample (b0063, b0087, b0094).
